intro: Most people in Bonnyrigg start thinking seriously about a wet room when a family member's mobility changes, or when a tired old bathroom finally reaches the end of its life. A wet room — a fully waterproofed, level-access shower space — offers a genuinely practical upgrade that works for all ages and lifestyles. Done properly, it adds real value to your home and transforms your daily routine. Whether you're adapting a bathroom for an elderly parent or simply want a sleek, modern space, Bonnyrigg homeowners are increasingly choosing wet rooms over conventional shower enclosures, and it's easy to see why when you look at the results.
localContext: Bonnyrigg's housing stock is genuinely varied, and that variety matters when planning a wet room installation. Older stone-built properties and period cottages — common throughout the town, particularly in the older residential streets — present specific challenges. Stone walls can be uneven, floors may not be level, and some older properties have timber subfloors that need careful assessment before any waterproofing work begins. Modern estate homes on the outskirts of Bonnyrigg are generally more straightforward, with concrete floors and more predictable layouts, but they still require a thorough survey before work starts. It's also worth knowing that Bonnyrigg sits in a moderately hard water area. While not as severe as parts of southern England, limescale can still gradually affect shower fittings, pumps, and screen seals over time — so it's worth discussing water-resistant fixture choices and potentially a small inline scale reducer with your installer from the outset.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Bonnyrigg typically follows a clear sequence of stages, each of which matters for the long-term performance of the finished space. The process begins with a detailed survey — your installer should visit in person to assess the floor structure, existing drainage position, wall materials, and whether the space needs tanking or a full wetroom former system. For older stone-built homes especially, this survey stage is not optional; what's behind the walls genuinely affects the approach. Once the plan is agreed, the existing bathroom is stripped out completely. Any timber subfloor is either reinforced or replaced, and the drainage point is set — this usually means cutting into the floor to position a linear or centre drain at the correct fall gradient. The entire floor and lower walls are then tanked using a specialist waterproof membrane, applied in multiple coats with sealed joints at every corner and pipe penetration. This tanking stage is arguably the most important part of the whole job — cut corners here and you'll have a leak within a year or two. After tanking, floor tiles are laid to a precise gradient so water flows naturally to the drain. Wall tiles or panels are fitted, the shower valve and head are plumbed in, and any screen or part-partition is installed. Finishing touches — sealant, fixtures, and a final inspection — complete the job. From strip-out to handover, most Bonnyrigg wet room installations take between five and eight working days.
pricing: In Bonnyrigg, a straightforward wet room conversion in a standard-sized bathroom typically costs between £6,000 and £9,000, including all labour, waterproofing, tiling, and a mid-range shower system. More complex projects — particularly in older stone properties where floors need significant structural work, or where premium fixtures and large-format tiles are specified — can reach £10,000 to £12,000 or beyond. The single biggest cost variables are the floor construction (timber subfloors cost more to prepare than concrete), the quality of the tile and drain specification, and whether any plumbing rerouting is needed. Always get a fixed written quote rather than an estimate before work begins.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Bonnyrigg and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely makes a difference on a job like this. A local installer will have worked in similar stone-built and period properties before — they'll know how to handle unexpected discoveries behind old walls without panicking or inflating costs on the spot. They're also more likely to have established relationships with local tile suppliers and plumbing merchants, which can help with lead times and getting the right materials quickly. Local tradespeople also have a local reputation to protect, which tends to concentrate the mind when it comes to quality.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built Bonnyrigg property?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more care than a modern home. Stone walls need to be assessed for stability and moisture, and timber ground floors often need reinforcing or replacing before waterproofing can be applied. A proper survey beforehand is essential. Most experienced installers working in Bonnyrigg will be familiar with these challenges and factor them into their quote from the start.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Bonnyrigg?
faqs.a: Most installations take between five and eight working days from strip-out to completion, depending on the size of the room and whether any structural work is needed. Older properties with uneven floors or tricky plumbing layouts sometimes add a day or two. Your installer should give you a realistic programme before work starts so you can plan around losing bathroom access.

faqs.q: Will limescale from Bonnyrigg's water supply affect my wet room?
faqs.a: Bonnyrigg has moderately hard water, so some limescale build-up on shower heads and glass screens is likely over time. It's manageable with regular cleaning and the right products, but it's worth discussing fixture choices — thermostatic valves and quality shower heads with easy-clean nozzles make maintenance easier. Some homeowners also add a small inline scale inhibitor to the supply to reduce build-up on fittings.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a Bonnyrigg home?
faqs.a: A well-installed wet room generally adds value, particularly if it replaces a tired or impractical bathroom. In Bonnyrigg's mix of period cottages and modern estate homes, a quality wet room can be a strong selling point — especially for buyers thinking about long-term accessibility. The key word is 'well-installed'; a poorly waterproofed room that develops leaks will do the opposite, so quality workmanship really matters here.
